examples.signature: Turn the Ship of Theseus puzzle from a surprising story into explicit rival identity principles, reasons, and a counterexample pressure test
Separate the empirical fact of a broken promise from the normative question of whether keeping promises is required, then build an argument rather than assert a preference
Use the question of whether an artificial system could be conscious to distinguish conceptual, empirical, metaphysical, and logical subquestions without pretending one method answers all of them

Transform the open question of whether universities should use AI proctoring into a qualified normative claim, explicit empirical and normative premises, and a conclusion without hiding disagreement inside vague words
Reconstruct a short paragraph about memory and personal identity by separating the author's conclusion, supporting reason, background assumption, and a premise that would need independent defense
Compare an argument for carrying an umbrella with an explanation of why the pavement is wet to distinguish support for accepting a claim from an account of why an accepted fact occurred
